races.title: State House, District 85
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Dudley Greene
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 85 (Avery, McDowell and Mitchell counties) since 2021. Career law enforcement officer: NC Alcohol Law Enforcement, Newland police, Avery and McDowell County sheriff's offices. Sheriff of McDowell County 2008-2018.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Greene was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no documented statements or actions from him on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, gun laws, abortion or education. His sponsored-bill list did not appear in the pages we could read. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026, so we have no self-described positions. We found no endorsements, controversies or foreign ties for him.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Career law enforcement officer (NC Alcohol Law Enforcement, Avery County chief deputy/chief detective). Sheriff of McDowell County 2008-2018, appointed and then re-elected twice. State House member since January 2021.
qual.why: He has held both local elected office and a legislative seat for several years. His career is in law enforcement rather than law, policy or budget work, which keeps him below the top band. Committee roles were not counted.

cands.name: Suzanne Gavenus
cands.bio: Licensed clinical social worker and Director of Counseling and Wellness at the NC School of Science and Math (NCSSM) in Morganton. Longtime Burnsville resident who previously lived in Avery County. Democratic candidate for NC House District 85 in 2026. No elected office held.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Suzanne Gavenus was born or raised, or when she first came to North Carolina. We found no statements from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, immigration enforcement or H-1B visas, policing, gun policy, or abortion. Her campaign materials mention land-use planning and affordable housing only in the context of Hurricane Helene recovery, with no specific growth or development positions. She has held no public office, so there are no actions in office to report.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Licensed clinical social worker. She describes herself on her campaign site as a behavioral health clinician, supervisor and administrator, and she is currently Director of Counseling and Wellness at NCSSM. She has held no elected office.
qual.why: She has a long career with management and administrative duties, but it is in clinical and school counseling rather than law, policy, budget work or elected service. She has no legislative experience.
qual.label: She has a long career with management and administrative duties, but it is in clinical and school counseling rather than law, policy, budget work or elected service. She has no legislative experience.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says she supports competitive, sustainable teacher pay with raises that keep up with inflation, and full funding for public schools. It does not mention vouchers, charters or school choice, and gives no 25% figure.
